title: T1052.001 — Exfiltration Over Physical Medium - Exfiltration over USB
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Exfiltration Over Physical Medium - Exfiltration over USB with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: T1052.001 - Exfiltration Over Physical Medium - Exfiltration over USB

steps.title: Two disconnected worlds
steps.caption: The picture starts quiet. An internet segment and an air-gapped segment sit side by side with no route between them. A clean USB stick waits in the middle. Evidence: none; silence is the baseline
steps.defender: nothing at all - both networks sit inside their normal baseline, and no sensor can see the gap that is about to be crossed.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Malware waits on both sides
steps.caption: Two small implants are already resident: one on the air-gapped host, one on the drop host. Neither calls out to the internet. Each simply polls for a newly mounted volume, in the style of the USBStealer toolset. Evidence: rare service (Sysmon 13), first-seen binary in AppData
steps.defender: a rare service registered on both hosts and a first-seen binary running from AppData - weak signals that are easy to miss without baseline tooling.

steps.title: The stick goes in (air-gapped side)
steps.caption: A person plugs the stick into the air-gapped host. The implant wakes, enumerates the volumes, and reads the staged documents folder on the air-gapped file server over the isolated LAN (local area network). E:\ . Evidence: USBSTOR registry write (Sysmon 13), hidden process reading the volume

steps.title: Files packed into a hidden container
steps.caption: The implant copies the staged files and packs them into a single container encrypted with XOR (a simple, reversible cipher) and given an odd extension - the "hidenc" pattern reported for USBStealer. Dozens of file writes land on the removable volume within seconds. Evidence: Sysmon 11 burst on E:\ , odd file extension
steps.defender: a sharp burst of Sysmon Event 11 file-create events on the removable volume, with an extension nobody has seen before.

steps.title: The courier walks
steps.caption: The person picks up the stick and walks across the room - or across the world. The gap is crossed by shoes, not packets. Evidence: none - the gap in telemetry is itself the clue
steps.defender: nothing, anywhere. No log, no alert, no flow record. This silence is the defining problem of T1052.001 and the reason correlation matters so much.

steps.title: The container leaves the network
steps.caption: The drop host uploads the container to the attacker server over HTTPS. To the proxy it looks like a normal web upload. Evidence: proxy upload record, rare destination domain
steps.defender: a large upload to a rare domain, starting shortly after USB activity on the same host.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC connects the dots
steps.caption: The SIEM joins the two USBSTOR records by device serial: the same physical drive touched two hosts within 48 hours. A case opens, responders pull both host timelines plus the proxy record, and device control is tightened on both segments. Evidence: same-serial-on-two-hosts correlation alert, device-control policy change
steps.defender: the correlation alert that finally makes the invisible relay visible.
